RESPONSE TO OWNER / REVIEW UPDATE:
Dear Dr. Wiltshire (or the hospital manager who ran your response through an AI tool):

Your reply is transparent corporate nonsense salted with a few bitter human edits. A real "old school" vet doesn't copy-paste sterile marketing lines about "continuing education and state-of-the-art equipment" while trying to justify a run down building and trash strewn all over the outside.

You claim I'm "dictating medicine," but my clinical advocacy saved my dog. Your junior vet dismissed his condition as a superficial "textbook hot spot", provided me with a useless topical spray, and didn't think a culture was necessary. I insisted on it, and the lab results 5 days later proved me 100% right—it was a deep bacterial infection requiring targeted antibiotics. If I hadn't forced your team to do their job, my 116-lb beloved dog would still be suffering from your incompetence.

As for your 1977 building with foundation issues? Stop using it as a folksy excuse for your high prices. Case in point: I just took my other dog to different vet clinica for the exact same hotspot care and was charged $133, while Lakeside charged me a staggering $600. This clinic is backed by private equity. We all know the corporate playbook: investors buy local practices, keep the old name on the sign for optics, let the physical infrastructure rot, and squeeze pet owners to hit profit margins.
Don't lecture me about your Google reviews - I suspect that they are fake, which is quite common now Our dog, who, by the way, is a highly-trained service animal, is getting his medicine because I knew better than your staff—despite your best efforts to miss the diagnosis.

Here is my original review:
My Experience: A Dilapidated Facility, Substandard Care, Predatory Billing, and Fake Positive Reviews

I originally chose this clinic based on Dr. Wilshire’s old-school, Texas A& M Veterinary School reputation, but with him out of town, my experience was incredibly disappointing. As a clinical social worker, I see how businesses impact vulnerable people. In my professional opinion, this clinic operates with a cold, transactional approach that prioritizes profit over proper care, taking financial advantage of people when their pets are hurting.

Suspicious Reviews: There is a staggering disconnect between their polished online rating and reality. I strongly suspect their 4.8-star rating is artificially padded. Do not let the stars fool you like they did me.

Run-Down & Chaotic: The exterior looks completely neglected and abandoned (see attached picture). Inside, the tiny waiting room is poorly managed. They allowed a large, unneutered dog to block the only exit, creating a high-stress hazard for hurting animals.

Medical Incompetence & Breed Ignorance: My 116lb Akbash (a livestock guardian breed) had a severe staph infection. The inexperienced vet dismissed my assessment, called it a "hotspot," refused to consult a senior vet, and forced him into an outdated plastic neck cone. Clamping a plastic dish on a guardian breed blindfolds their peripheral vision and is incredibly inhumane (see photo).

Outrageous, Predatory Billing: They charged me $600 for a basic exam and severe under-treatment. By the next day, because he wasn't given systemic oral meds, his face deteriorated into a bleeding, ulcerated crater (see before/after pics). When I returned to get the correct medications from a senior doctor, they actually tried to charge me a second time for a crisis caused entirely by their own initial failure.

Final Verdict:
In my opinion, this clinic is unkempt, uneducated on working breeds, and uses predatory billing practices that do a disservice to the community. Take your animals, your medical records, and your money to a modern, competent facility.

My one year old cat had ringworm. I took him to see the vet in the clinic. They prescribed him Itrafungol. They didn't warn me that I needed to watch my cat's eating habits. My cat finished 2/3 of the bottle of the medication. All of sudden he stopped eating for four days. I took him to the clinic. They told me he might have liver issues. Last time I took him for ringworm diagnosis.They told me my cat was very healthy. Today I took him to the clinic. They told me my cat is very sick. I asked them my cat has been really healthy and lively why all of sudden he has liver issue. He is only one year old.  I asked them if it has anything to do with Itrafungol. They said it is possible. I came home and check Itrafungol. I realized it has very strong side effects on the liver of the cat and I should have stopped feeding him the medication on the third time. I am a bit disappointed that the clinic never mentioned that to me. To me, it feels like the ringworm hasn't gone completely now my cat developed other issues.
